# Mono-White Angels

- **Format:** Casual 60-card, 1v1
- **Archetype:** Flyers + lifegain midrange: Angels race in the air, and the life you gain powers up Righteous Valkyrie, Angel of Vitality and Exemplar of Light
- **Played by:** either. Suits whoever likes flying creatures, attacking every turn and watching their life total climb. It's the simpler of the two decks.
- **Status:** idea
- **Paired against:** [Mono-Black Zombies](mono-black-zombies.md)
- **Complexity:** 2.5/5
- **Estimated power:** 6 with owned cards only, 6.5 with the buys (on a 1v1 scale)
- **Configuration:** **Now** set, pair 1. Builds alongside Izzet and Gruul. It uses 23 cards from the Calling All Angels precon, so it and the Giada Commander deck can't both be built at once.

A flying army of Angels that gains life as it goes. You play a cheap Angel on turn 2 and a bigger one most turns after that, attacking over the top of ground creatures. The life you gain powers up Righteous Valkyrie (+2/+2 to your whole team at 27 life), Angel of Vitality and Exemplar of Light. Lyra Dawnbringer, Linvala and Archangel of Tithes finish the game. It suits a player who likes attacking every turn and watching their life total go up, and it has fewer fiddly activated abilities than the Zombies.

### Why these buys (in priority order)

1. **3x Luminarch Aspirant** (replaces Metropolis Reformer, Firemane Commando, Norn's Choirmaster). The best white 2-drop in the list. At the beginning of combat on each of your turns it puts a +1/+1 counter on one creature you control (usually a flyer), so your team gets one counter bigger every turn and the Zombies must answer it. A counter on Exemplar of Light also draws a card. In testing it was the single biggest upgrade in the package. No reprint is announced. *Also useful in: Giada Commander deck (Calling All Angels upgrade); any white creature deck (Finneas Rabbits, Orzhov).*
2. **2x Youthful Valkyrie** (replaces 1 Angel of Vitality, 1 Plains (target runs 22 lands)). Takes the deck to 4 copies of a cheap 2-mana flyer that grows each time another Angel enters, so more games start on turn 2. Reprinted in FDC 2026 (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait. Only 1 copy was in stock at MTGMate's cheapest price (A$0.80) on 2026-09-28, so the second may cost more. *Also useful in: Giada Commander (the precon already has 1).*
3. **2x Journey to Nowhere** (replaces 2 Valorous Stance). Exiles any creature for 2 mana. Valorous Stance only kills toughness 4+, and most Zombies are small. Exile also stops Zombie recursion and death triggers (Headless Rider, Undead Augur, Gravecrawler). No reprint is announced. *Also useful in: Giada Commander; Orzhov Removal; any white deck.*
4. **1x Inspiring Overseer** (replaces Grasp of Fate). A 4th copy of a 3-mana flyer that replaces itself (gain 1 life, draw a card). Cheap: A$1.00 at MTGMate on 2026-09-28. Reprinted in FDC 2026 (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait. *Also useful in: Every white deck (Orzhov Removal, Finneas Rabbits, Giada Commander).*

## Substitutes

The owned list (buildable once the precon arrives on 2 Oct) plays these cards until the target buys arrive:

| Target buy | Owned card played until it arrives | What the swap costs |
|---|---|---|
| 3x Luminarch Aspirant | Metropolis Reformer, Firemane Commando, Norn's Choirmaster | The biggest gap. These are decent flyers, but they don't grow your team every turn. This swap is about half of the upgrade's value. |
| 2x Youthful Valkyrie (3rd and 4th copies) | 1x Angel of Vitality, 1x Plains (owned list runs 23 lands) | Small: a few more slow starts, and slightly more flood. |
| 2x Journey to Nowhere | 2x Valorous Stance | Small to medium. Stance can't kill Zombies with toughness 3 or less, but it can also make an Angel indestructible in response to Go for the Throat or Hero's Downfall. |
| 1x Inspiring Overseer (4th copy) | Grasp of Fate | Small. Grasp is flexible removal (it can also exile Liliana's Mastery), while Overseer is a flyer that draws a card. |

Simulated head-to-head: the owned Angels vs the owned Zombies win about 51-53% (two simulator runs). The target Angels vs the owned Zombies win about 62-63%, so **buy both decks' packages together** (see the head-to-head section below).

## Notes

### How the deck wins
- Play an Angel almost every turn from turn 2 and attack in the air. **Flying** means only creatures with flying or reach can block it. The Zombies have one such blocker at most (Vampire Nighthawk), so your attacks usually get through.
- Gain life along the way: Bishop of Wings (+4 per Angel), Dazzling Angel, Righteous Valkyrie, Inspiring Overseer and Seraph Sanctuary. Life isn't just a buffer:
  - At **25+ life**, Angel of Vitality becomes a 4/4.
  - At **27+ life** (7 above your starting 20), Righteous Valkyrie gives **all** your creatures +2/+2.
- The finishers:
  - **Lyra Dawnbringer:** 5/5 flying, first strike, lifelink, and your other Angels get +1/+1 and lifelink.
  - **Linvala:** a 5/5 flyer that catches you up if you're behind.
  - **Archangel of Tithes:** while it's **untapped**, your opponent must pay 1 mana for each creature that attacks you (and while it attacks, they must pay 1 for each creature that blocks). It has no vigilance, so if you attack with it, the attack tax is off during their next turn.
- Spend your removal on **lords**, the Zombies that make other Zombies bigger: Death Baron, Lord of the Accursed, Lord of the Undead, Cemetery Reaper and Undead Warchief. Save something for Grave Titan if you can.

### Opening hand and mulligans
- **Keep** 7 cards with **2 to 5 lands** and at least one creature you can cast by turn 3 (Giada, Youthful Valkyrie, Luminarch Aspirant, Bishop of Wings, Inspiring Overseer, Dazzling Angel).
- **Mulligan** hands with 0-1 or 6-7 lands, or where everything costs 5 or more. To mulligan: shuffle, draw a new 7, then put 1 card on the bottom for each mulligan you've taken.
- A 2-land hand with 2-drops is fine, especially when you go second (on the draw).

### Play tips
1. **Race in the air; don't trade on the ground.** Death Baron gives Zombies **deathtouch**: any damage they deal destroys the creature. Blocking them with a good Angel is usually a bad trade, so only block to stay alive, or with cheap creatures.
2. **First strike beats deathtouch.** Lyra, Norn's Choirmaster (owned list) and any creature wearing Angelic Destiny deal their damage first. If that first-strike damage is enough to kill the deathtouch Zombie they fight, it dies before it can hit back.
3. **Legend rule.** Giada and Lyra are *legendary*: you can only control one of each at a time. Keep the second copy in hand until the first one dies. The Zombies have lots of removal, so it will.
4. **Giada's mana.** Tap Giada for an extra white mana that can only be spent on Angels. She has **vigilance** (attacking doesn't tap her), so she can attack first and still tap for mana after combat. She also makes each new Angel enter with one extra +1/+1 counter for each Angel you already control (Giada counts herself).
5. **Court of Grace** makes you the **monarch**: you draw an extra card at the end of each of your turns, and at the start of each of your turns Court makes a 4/4 flying Angel (only a 1/1 flying Spirit if you're not the monarch). But if a Zombie deals combat damage to you, *they* become the monarch. Play Court when you have blockers or Archangel of Tithes, not when a wide Zombie board is about to hit you.
6. **Angel of Finality** exiles a graveyard. Aim it at the Zombie player to stop Gravecrawler, Zul Ashur and Lord of the Undead bringing Zombies back.
7. **Exemplar of Light** draws a card the first time each turn it gets +1/+1 counters, for any reason: gaining life, Luminarch Aspirant's counter, or entering with Giada's counters.
8. **Norn's Choirmaster** (owned list): its proliferate ability only works with a commander, so in this deck it's simply a 5/4 flyer with first strike.

### Cards to watch out for (Zombies)
- **Death Baron and the other lords.** Every lord makes all their Zombies bigger, and lords also pump each other.
- **Removal:** they have about 11 removal spells (Deathmark kills any white creature for 1 mana; Go for the Throat, Hero's Downfall, Consuming Corruption). Don't pile everything onto one Angel. Spread your threats, and put Angelic Destiny on a creature that's already done its job.
- **Gray Merchant of Asphodel:** when it enters, you lose life equal to their **devotion to black** (the number of black mana symbols in the mana costs of their permanents). Keep your life high.
- **Grave Titan:** a 6/6 deathtouch that makes two 2/2 Zombies when it enters and every time it attacks.
- **Feed the Swarm and Withering Torment** can destroy Stasis Snare, Journey to Nowhere or Grasp of Fate (the exiled creature comes back), or Court of Grace.
- **Vampire Nighthawk** (owned Zombies list only): a flying deathtouch lifelink blocker that kills any Angel it fights, unless the Angel has first strike and deals it at least 3 damage first.

### Sideboard: vs stronger opponents
These cards are kept out of the Zombies matchup because they're one-sided or too swingy. Against a stronger opponent, swap them in one-for-one (stay at 60 cards):
- **Sunblast Angel** destroys all *tapped* creatures, **yours included**. Cast it on your turn after he has attacked with creatures that lack vigilance (they stay tapped), and before you attack.
- **Austere Command:** choose the two modes that hurt him more than you. Careful: "enchantments" also destroys your own Stasis Snare and Journey to Nowhere (his creatures come back) and your Court of Grace, and each creature mode hits your Angels of that mana value too.
- Bring Sunblast Angel and Austere Command in against creature-heavy decks, for Valorous Stance x2 (or Journey to Nowhere in the target list).
- **Sephara, Sky's Blade:** a 7/7 flying lifelink bomb. You can cast her for just {W} by tapping four untapped creatures with flying. Bring her in for Norn's Choirmaster (or an Angel of Vitality).
- **Angel of the Ruins** and **Invoke the Divine:** against artifacts and enchantments. Bring them in for Metropolis Reformer and Grasp of Fate (target list: for Angel of Finality and Devout Decree).
- **Devout Decree** only hits black or red creatures. If his deck has neither, it's a dead card, so swap it out first.
- **Knight of Grace:** against black decks, *but not the Zombies*, where it proved unfairly strong. Bring it in for an Angel of Vitality.

### Head-to-head vs Mono-Black Zombies (tested)

**Verdict: close to a coin flip**, about 53/47 Angels with the owned lists and 51/49 with the buys.

| Angels win % | Original simulator | Re-checked simulator |
|---|---|---|
| Owned vs owned | 50–52% | 52–54% |
| Both with buys | 51% | 51–52% |
| Angels with buys, Zombies owned | 63% | 62% |
| Angels owned, Zombies with buys | 42% | 40% |

**How it was tested.** A rules simulator written for this pair played 5,000–8,000 games per matchup, alternating who goes first. An independent re-check compared every card's code with its Scryfall text, fixed five small gaps (for example Cryptbreaker's draw ability and Exemplar of Light's card draw) and re-ran 2 × 6,000 games. Another 19 games were played by hand from random deals: Angels 11, Zombies 8, and most were decided by mana problems.

**Going first** matters little: the player going first wins about 52% (the Angels win 53% of the games they start, the Zombies 51%).

#### Why it's even
- It's a race between the air and the ground. The Angels fly over a deck with almost no flying blockers. The Zombies' lords and Death Baron's deathtouch make every block the Angels make a bad trade.
- The Zombies' 11 removal spells answer the Angels' best cards. The Angels' 9–10 include exile, which stops Zombie recursion.
- Lyra Dawnbringer is the biggest single swing (about +20 points in games where she's drawn), but she can be answered. The colour-hoser removal is symmetric (Devout Decree against Deathmark). Both Knights and every one-sided sweeper stay in the sideboards.
- **Angels win** when their flyers and lifegain get ahead, or Lyra or Angelic Destiny sticks. **Zombies win** by curving 1-drop, 2-drop, lord, killing the key flyer, then draining with Gray Merchant.

#### Buying rule
Each deck's Tier-1 package is worth about 10 points, so upgrade both decks together. You can also buy in two matched steps: (1) Luminarch Aspirant ×3 with Graveyard Marshal ×3 (tested at 50%), then (2) the rest of both packages. On 2026-09-28 MTGMate had only 1 Luminarch Aspirant (of 3), so find the other two at Good Games or the local shop. Keep both decks on their owned lists until both packages are complete, then swap them in on the same day.

#### Tuning levers (one swap at a time)
- **If the Angels win too often:** Court of Grace → Always Watching (about −2 points, and simpler), or 1 Lyra → Herald of Faith (about −3 to −4).
- **If the Zombies win too often:** move Knight of Grace from the Angels' sideboard into the main deck (about +4 for the Angels, the biggest swing).
- **Not a lever:** giving the Zombies Kalitas, Bad Moon or Graveborn Muse in place of Wight of Precinct Six makes them 2–3 points *weaker* (55.5–56.5% Angels).
- **Tier-2 buys:** match each one with a similar upgrade for the other deck.

Simulator code and full game logs from the 2026-09-28 analysis are not kept in the repo.
